It has also been said ﴿المُضْعِفُونَ﴾, as one says ”رَجُلٌ مَقْوٍ“, i.e. possessed of strength, and ”مُوسِرٌ“, i.e. possessed of wealth; likewise ”مُضْعِفٌ“, i.e. possessed of multiples of good deeds.

zajjaj:41-41.t: His saying, Exalted is He: ”ظَهَرَ الفَسادُ في البَرِّ والبَحْرِ بِما كَسَبَتْ أيْدِي النّاسِ لِيُذِيقَهم بَعْضَ الَّذِي عَمِلُوا“ — and it is also read with yāʾ: ﴿لِيُذِيقَهُمْ﴾ [Translator's note: so in the source; both forms quoted are with yāʾ — the first quotation was presumably meant as «لِنُذِيقَهم», with nūn]. I.e. that He may make them taste the recompense of some of their deeds. Its meaning: drought appeared on land, and dearth at sea, i.e. in the cities of the sea, i.e. in the cities that are on rivers; and everything that has water is a "sea" (baḥr).

zajjaj:43-43.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فَأقِمْ وجْهَكَ لِلدِّينِ القَيِّمِ مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يَأْتِيَ يَوْمٌ لا مَرَدَّ لَهُ مِنَ اللَّهِ يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصَّدَّعُونَ﴾ — the meaning of ”فَأقِمْ وجْهَكَ“ is: set your aim straight, and make your direction the following of the upright religion, before the Hour comes and the Resurrection takes place, when no soul's faith will benefit it if it had not believed before or earned some good through its faith. The meaning of ”يَوْمَئِذٍ يَصَّدَّعُونَ“ is: they will separate, becoming a party in Paradise and a party in the Blaze.

zajjaj:44-44.t:
His saying: ﴿فَلأنْفُسِهِمْ يَمْهَدُونَ﴾ — i.e. they are preparing [a resting place] for themselves.
His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَلَئِنْ أرْسَلْنا رِيحًا فَرَأوْهُ مُصْفَرًّا﴾ [al-Rūm: 51] — i.e. they saw the vegetation had turned yellow and dried up; ﴿لَظَلُّوا مِن بَعْدِهِ يَكْفُرُونَ﴾ [al-Rūm: 51] — and its meaning is ”لِيَظَلُّنَّ“ (they would surely remain) [Translator's note: so vocalised in the source; the intended form is presumably «لَيَظَلُّنَّ»], because the sense of the speech is condition and recompense. So they rejoice at the rain, and disbelieve when the rain is cut off from them and the vegetation dries up.

zajjaj:48-48.t:
His saying: ﴿وَيَجْعَلُهُ كِسَفًا﴾ — i.e. pieces of cloud.
His saying: ﴿فَتَرى الوَدْقَ يَخْرُجُ مِن خِلالِهِ﴾ — i.e. you see the rain coming out from the gaps of the cloud. So He, Mighty and Majestic is He, made known that He produces the clouds, revives the earth and sends the winds, and all that is proof of the power which created beings are incapable of, and that He is able to give life to the dead.

zajjaj:49-49.t:
His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿وَإنْ كانُوا مِن قَبْلِ أنْ يُنَـزَّلَ عَلَيْهِمْ مِن قَبْلِهِ لَمُبْلِسِينَ﴾ — the meaning is "before the rain is sent down upon them"; and it is read ”أنْ يَنْزِلَ“ (before it comes down). The meaning of ”مُبْلِسِينَ“ is: cut short with the cutting short of those who despair. As for the repetition of His saying ”مِن قَبْلِ“, there are two aspects in it. Quṭrub said: the first ”قَبْلِ“ is for the sending down, and the second ”قَبْلِ“ is for the rain. Al-Akhfash and others of the Basrans said: the repetition of ”قَبْلِ“ is by way of tawkīd (emphasis), and the meaning is: "and indeed, before the sending down of the rain, they were in despair." The view is as they said, because the sending down of the rain is in the sense of the rain, since rain only comes about through being sent down, just as winds are only known through their passing. The poet said:
مَشَيْنَ كَما اهْتَزَّتْ رِماحٌ تَسَفَّهَتْ ∗∗∗ أعالِيَها مَرُّ الرِّياحِ النَّواسِمِ
(They walked [swaying] as spears quiver whose tops the passing of the gentle breezes has set swaying.)
So the meaning of ”مَرُّ الرِّياحِ“ is like your saying ”تَسَفَّهَتْ أعالِيَها مَرُّ الرِّياحِ النَّواسِمِ“. [Translator's note: the explanation repeats the verse's own wording; the point intended is that "the passing of the winds" stands for "the winds".]

zajjaj:50-50.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿فانْظُرْ إلى آثارِ رَحْمَتِ اللَّهِ﴾ — and it is read ”أثَرِ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ“ (the trace of Allah's mercy). He means the traces of the rain, which is a mercy from Allah — how He revives the earth after its death, and its revival is His making it put forth vegetation; and likewise is the revival of the dead. So He said: ﴿إنَّ ذَلِكَ لَمُحْيِي المَوْتى﴾ — ”ذَلِكَ“ is a reference to Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He.

zajjaj:52-52.t: His saying: ﴿فَإنَّكَ لا تُسْمِعُ المَوْتى ولا تُسْمِعُ الصُّمَّ الدُّعاءَ إذا ولَّوْا مُدْبِرِينَ﴾ — this is a likeness which Allah struck for the unbelievers, as He said: ﴿صُمٌّ بُكْمٌ عُمْيٌ﴾ [al-Baqara: 18]. So He made them, in their failing to act upon what they hear and to heed what they see, as the dead; because what He has made clear of His power and His making, the like of which created beings are not able to do, is proof of His Oneness.

zajjaj:53-53.t:
His saying: ﴿إنْ تُسْمِعُ إلا مَن يُؤْمِنُ بِآياتِنا﴾ — i.e. none hears except one who believes in Our signs. He made "causing to hear" here count as causing to hear when it is accepted and what is heard is acted upon; and when it is not accepted it is as what has not been heard and not been seen.
His saying: ﴿وَما أنْتَ بِهادِ العُمْيِ عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ﴾ — the reading is with the genitive in ”اَلْعُمْيِ“, and the accusative is permissible: ”بِهادٍ العُمْيَ عَنْ ضَلالَتِهِمْ“. The reading is with the genitive. As for the accusative, if there is a transmission for it [then so be it]; otherwise reading with it is not permissible, because anything that is recited without there being a prior transmission for it from the early readers of the cities — reciting with it is an innovation, even if it is permissible in Arabic. The practice in all recitation is following the Sunna.

zajjaj:54-54.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكم مِن ضَعْفٍ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِن بَعْدِ ضَعْفٍ قُوَّةً ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِن بَعْدِ قُوَّةٍ ضَعْفًا وشَيْبَةً يَخْلُقُ ما يَشاءُ﴾ — its interpretation is that He created you from sperm-drops in a state of weakness, then strengthened you in the state of youth, then after youth made weakness and grey hair. It is related in the ḥadīth «that Ibn ʿUmar said: I recited to the Prophet ﷺ ﴿اللَّهُ الَّذِي خَلَقَكم مِن ضَعْفٍ﴾, and he had me recite ”مِن ضُعْفٍ“. And ʿAṭiyya recited to Ibn ʿUmar ”مِن ضَعْفٍ“, and he had him recite ”مِن ضُعْفٍ“ and said to him: "I recited it to the Prophet ﷺ as ”مِن ضَعْفٍ“,» and he had me recite ”مِن ضُعْفٍ“." So what ʿAṭiyya related from Ibn ʿUmar from the Prophet ﷺ is ”مِن ضُعْفٍ“, with ḍamma. It has also been read with fatḥa on the ḍād, and the preferred choice is the ḍamma, because of the transmission.

zajjaj:55-55.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَيَوْمَ تَقُومُ السّاعَةُ يُقْسِمُ المُجْرِمُونَ﴾ — He means the Day of Resurrection. ”اَلسّاعَةُ“ in the Qur'an has the meaning of the hour in which the Resurrection takes place; for that reason He left out any mention identifying which hour it is. ﴿يُقْسِمُ المُجْرِمُونَ﴾ — the criminals swear; ﴿ما لَبِثُوا غَيْرَ ساعَةٍ﴾ — i.e. they did not remain in their graves except a single hour; ﴿كَذَلِكَ كانُوا يُؤْفَكُونَ﴾ — i.e. like this lie was their lying [in the world], because they swore without verification.

zajjaj:56-56.t: His saying, Mighty and Majestic is He: ﴿وَقالَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا العِلْمَ والإيمانَ لَقَدْ لَبِثْتُمْ في كِتابِ اللَّهِ إلى يَوْمِ البَعْثِ﴾ — i.e. in the knowledge of Allah, recorded in the Preserved Tablet.

zajjaj:60-60.t: His saying: ﴿فاصْبِرْ إنَّ وعْدَ اللَّهِ حَقٌّ﴾ — i.e. what Allah has promised you of victory over your enemy is true, and the manifestation of the religion of Islam is true. ﴿وَلا يَسْتَخِفَّنَّكَ الَّذِينَ لا يُوقِنُونَ﴾ — i.e. "Let not those who have no certainty unsettle you from your religion," i.e. they are astray and in doubt.
